title: The imperfect subjunctive: hablara, comiera, viviera
summary: Form the imperfect subjunctive from the ellos preterite, in -ra and -se, and use it for far-fetched wishes with ojalá and the polite quisiera.
focus: Forming the imperfect subjunctive; ojalá + imperfect subjunctive and quisiera
content:
## Built from the ellos preterite

The imperfect subjunctive has no new stems to learn. Take the **ellos** form of the preterite, drop **-ron**, and add the endings: **hablaron → hablara**, **comieron → comiera**, **vivieron → viviera**. Every verb also has a second set in **-se**, shown after the dot. -er and -ir verbs share the same endings.

| | hablar | comer | vivir |
|---|---|---|---|
| yo | hablara · hablase | comiera · comiese | viviera · viviese |
| tú | hablaras · hablases | comieras · comieses | vivieras · vivieses |
| él / ella / usted | hablara · hablase | comiera · comiese | viviera · viviese |
| nosotros/as | habláramos · hablásemos | comiéramos · comiésemos | viviéramos · viviésemos |
| vosotros/as | hablarais · hablaseis | comierais · comieseis | vivierais · vivieseis |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | hablaran · hablasen | comieran · comiesen | vivieran · viviesen |

## Two endings, one tense

The **-ra** forms (*hablara*) and the **-se** forms (*hablase*) are both correct and mean the same in almost every use. **-ra** is the more common everywhere, especially in speech; **-se** is heard in Spain and in careful writing. Use one, recognise both.

Two details to watch:

- The **nosotros** form always carries a written accent, three syllables from the end: **habláramos, comiéramos, tuviéramos, fuésemos**. No other form has one.
- **yo** and **él / ella / usted** share a form, so add the subject when it is not clear: *Ojalá **yo** supiera…*, *Ojalá **ella** supiera…*

## Irregular stems come for free

Whatever is irregular in the ellos preterite carries straight over: know **tuvieron** and you already know **tuviera**.

| infinitive | ellos preterite | imperfect subjunctive |
|---|---|---|
| tener | tuvieron | tuviera |
| estar | estuvieron | estuviera |
| ser / ir | fueron | fuera |
| hacer | hicieron | hiciera |
| poder | pudieron | pudiera |
| poner | pusieron | pusiera |
| saber | supieron | supiera |
| querer | quisieron | quisiera |
| decir | dijeron | dijera |
| venir | vinieron | viniera |
| pedir | pidieron | pidiera |
| dormir | durmieron | durmiera |
| leer | leyeron | leyera |

The -se forms follow the same way (*tuviese, fuese, dijese*). Watch **dijeron → dijera** (no *i*) and the stem changes in **pidiera** and **durmiera**. **Fuera** is the form for both *ser* and *ir*, and context tells you which.

## Ojalá: likely or far-fetched

**Ojalá** (*I hope, if only*) always takes the subjunctive, and the tense tells the listener how likely you think the wish is.

- **Ojalá + present subjunctive**: it may well happen. *Ojalá llegue a tiempo.* (I hope she gets here on time.)
- **Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive**: unlikely or impossible, often about right now. *Ojalá tuviera tu edad.* (I wish I were your age.) *Ojalá no lloviera tanto aquí.* (If only it didn't rain so much here.)

The same wish can go either way: *Ojalá venga Ana* (she might come) against *Ojalá viniera Ana* (she almost certainly won't). A **que** after ojalá is optional: *ojalá que viniera*.

## Quisiera, and a first look at quería que

**Quisiera** (from *querer*) is the polite *I'd like*. It is softer than **quiero** and as courteous as **me gustaría**. In this use only the -ra form works, never *quisiese*.

- *Quisiera un kilo de tomates, por favor.* (I'd like a kilo of tomatoes, please.)
- *Quisiera hablar con el responsable.* (I'd like to speak to the person in charge.)

You will also meet the imperfect subjunctive after a main verb in the past. The next lesson covers it in full. For now, notice the pattern:

- *Quería que vinieras.* (I wanted you to come.)
- *Me pidió que lo hiciera.* (She asked me to do it.)

vocabulary.example: Ojalá fuera viernes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wish it were Friday.

vocabulary.example: Quisiera reservar una habitación para tres noches.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'd like to book a room for three nights.

vocabulary.example: Mi deseo era que todos estuvieran juntos en Navidad.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My wish was for everyone to be together at Christmas.

vocabulary.meaning: to win the lottery (la lotería le toca a alguien)
vocabulary.example: Ojalá nos tocara la lotería este año.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If only we won the lottery this year.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá dispusiéramos de más tiempo para el proyecto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wish we had more time for the project.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá me atreviera a cantar en público.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wish I dared to sing in public.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá cupiera todo en una sola maleta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If only everything fitted in a single suitcase.

vocabulary.example: Mis padres querían que nos mudáramos a Valencia.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My parents wanted us to move to Valencia.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá pudiera trabajar un año en el extranjero.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wish I could work abroad for a year.

vocabulary.example: Te echo de menos; ojalá estuvieras aquí.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I miss you; I wish you were here.

vocabulary.meaning: to listen to, pay attention to (advice)
vocabulary.example: Ojalá mi hermano me hiciera caso alguna vez.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If only my brother listened to me for once.

vocabulary.example: Quisiera hablar con usted sobre un aumento de sueldo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'd like to talk to you about a pay rise.

quiz.prompt: Tener: ellos tuvieron. Which is the yo form of the imperfect subjunctive?
quiz.explanation: Drop -ron from the ellos preterite tuvieron and add -ra: tuviera. The irregular stem tuv- carries over. Tendría is the conditional and tenía the imperfect indicative.
hints: Start from tuvieron, not from the infinitive.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá (nosotros) ___ más tiempo libre. (tener: I wish we had more free time)
quiz.explanation: Tuvieron gives tuvie- + -ramos = tuviéramos (or tuviésemos). The nosotros form carries a written accent. The imperfect subjunctive marks a wish you don't expect to come true.

quiz.prompt: It's August in Seville and forty degrees. You wish it were snowing right now: Ojalá ___.
quiz.explanation: Snow in Seville in August is impossible, so ojalá takes the imperfect subjunctive: ojalá nevara. Ojalá nieve would be a hope that could come true; nevaba is indicative and never follows ojalá.
hints: Unlikely or impossible wishes take the imperfect subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá me ___ la verdad. (decir, tú: I wish you'd tell me the truth)
quiz.explanation: Decir: ellos dijeron gives dije- + -ras = dijeras (or dijeses). Just as dijeron has no i, neither does dijeras.

quiz.prompt: In a shop, the polite way to ask: ___ ver esa chaqueta, por favor.
quiz.explanation: Quisiera is the courteous 'I'd like', as polite as me gustaría. Quiera is the present subjunctive and cannot start a request on its own; querré is the future.
hints: The polite form of querer comes from quisieron.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá todo ___ en el maletero. (caber: if only everything fitted in the boot)
quiz.explanation: Caber has an irregular preterite, cupieron. Drop -ron, add -ra: cupiera (or cupiese).
hints: The ellos preterite of caber is cupieron.

quiz.prompt: Mis padres querían que nos ___ a Valencia.
quiz.explanation: A main verb in the past (querían) is followed by the imperfect subjunctive: que nos mudáramos. The next lesson covers this pattern in full.
hints: The nosotros form has an accent: -áramos.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá me ___ a decírselo. (atreverse, yo: I wish I dared to tell him)
quiz.explanation: Atrevieron gives atrevie- + -ra = atreviera (or atreviese). The yo form is the same as the él form; me already shows who it is.

conversations.title: Monday wishes
conversations.scenario: Lucía and Javier share a coffee on a terrace in Madrid after a long Monday at the office.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Uf, lunes otra vez. Ojalá estuviéramos ya en agosto.
lines.meaning: Ugh, Monday again. I wish it were already August.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ya ves. Yo quisiera tomarme un año sabático.
lines.meaning: Tell me about it. I'd like to take a year off.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Really? And what would you do?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Viajar. Ojalá pudiera recorrer Sudamérica en moto.
lines.meaning: Travel. If only I could ride round South America on a motorbike.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Mis padres querían que estudiara Derecho, y aquí estoy, en una oficina.
lines.meaning: My parents wanted me to study law, and here I am, in an office.
lines.note: A past main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: And what did you want to be?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Fotógrafa. Ojalá me atreviera a cambiar de trabajo ahora.
lines.meaning: A photographer. I wish I dared to change jobs now.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Nunca es tarde. Ojalá encuentres algo que te guste.
lines.meaning: It's never too late. I hope you find something you like.
lines.note: ojalá with the present subjunctive: a real possibility

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Gracias. Bueno, quisiera otro café con leche.
lines.meaning: Thanks. Right, I'd like another white coffee.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Y yo una caña. Ojalá nos tocara la lotería y no volviéramos a la oficina.
lines.meaning: And a small beer for me. If only we won the lottery and never went back to the office.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Ojalá! Pero primero habría que comprar un décimo.
lines.meaning: If only! But first we'd have to buy a lottery ticket.
lines.note: un décimo: a tenth-share of a Spanish lottery ticket

listening.text: Ojalá hiciera menos calor.
listening.meaning: I wish it weren't so hot.

listening.text: Quisiera un billete para Toledo.
listening.meaning: I'd like a ticket to Toledo.

listening.text: Ojalá supiera tocar la guitarra.
listening.meaning: I wish I could play the guitar.

listening.text: Ojalá vinieras a la boda con nosotros.
listening.meaning: I wish you'd come to the wedding with us.
listening.note: New word: la boda = the wedding.

listening.text: Ojalá mis abuelos vivieran más cerca de nosotros.
listening.meaning: If only my grandparents lived closer to us.

listening.text: Quisiera hablar con la directora antes de la reunión.
listening.meaning: I'd like to speak to the director before the meeting.
listening.note: New word: la reunión = the meeting.

listening.text: Ojalá estuviéramos en la playa en lugar de en la oficina.
listening.meaning: I wish we were at the beach instead of at the office.
listening.note: Only the nosotros form has an accent: estuviéramos.

listening.text: El profesor quería que leyéramos el libro entero antes del examen.
listening.meaning: The teacher wanted us to read the whole book before the exam.

guide.tip: Stuck on a form? Say the ellos preterite out loud first (dijeron, pudieron, fueron), then swap -ron for -ra.

bites.title: From the ellos preterite
bites.rule: Take the ellos preterite, drop -ron, add -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -rais, -ran. hablaron → hablara; tuvieron → tuviera.
bites.example_meaning: I wish I had a dog.

bites.title: -ra or -se
bites.rule: Every verb has two sets: hablara or hablase. Both are correct and mean the same; -ra is the more common. Only nosotros has an accent: habláramos.
bites.example: Ojalá lo supiera. Ojalá lo supiese.
bites.example_meaning: I wish I knew. I wish I knew.

bites.title: Ojalá: hope or sigh
bites.rule: Ojalá with the present subjunctive means it may well happen. With the imperfect subjunctive it is unlikely or impossible, often about right now.
bites.example_meaning: I hope she comes. If only she would come.

bites.title: Quisiera means I'd like
bites.rule: Quisiera softens a request: politer than quiero, as polite as me gustaría. Use it in shops, offices and emails. Only the -ra form works here.
bites.example_meaning: I'd like to exchange this shirt.

sorts.title: Hope or sigh?

items.text: Ojalá llegue a tiempo el tren.
Ojalá haga buen tiempo el sábado.
Ojalá tuviera veinte años otra vez.

sorts.why: The present subjunctive says the speaker thinks it can happen; the imperfect subjunctive says it is a long shot or impossible.

sorts.title: Which tense is it?
sorts.why: -ra / -se forms are the imperfect subjunctive; -aba / -ía is the imperfect indicative; -ría is the conditional.

sorts.title: Same stem or new stem?
sorts.why: Regular verbs keep their stem; any change in the ellos preterite (tuvieron, dijeron, pusieron, durmieron) carries over.

spots.why: Only the nosotros form carries a written accent: tuviéramos.
Dijeron has no i after the j, so dijeras has none either.

spots.sentence: Ojalá pudieramos ir a la playa.
spots.why: The nosotros form always takes an accent: pudiéramos.
Built from the preterite hicieron, not from hacer.

builds.meaning: I wish I had more free time.
I'd like to ask you a favour.
If only it weren't so cold.

builds.text: Mi madre quería que la llamara.
builds.meaning: My mother wanted me to call her.

builds.text: Ojalá pudiéramos quedarnos aquí para siempre.
builds.meaning: I wish we could stay here forever.

realm.content:
## Deseos en Eldmark

Every adventurer sighs **ojalá**. **Ojalá tuviera** más pociones (you have none left) and **ojalá el dragón durmiera** (he is wide awake). The imperfect subjunctive marks a wish you hardly expect. At the inn, a well-bred hero never says *quiero*: **Quisiera** una habitación, por favor.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá el enano supiera leer este mapa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wish the dwarf could read this map.

vocabulary.example: Quisiera una habitación en la posada, por favor.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'd like a room at the inn, please.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá me atreviera a entrar en la mazmorra.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wish I dared to go into the dungeon.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá el botín cupiera en mi mochila.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If only the loot fitted in my backpack.

vocabulary.example: La elfa echa de menos el Bosque Umbrío; ojalá pudiera volver.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The elf misses the Bosque Umbrío; she wishes she could go back.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá el guerrero nos hiciera caso antes de atacar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If only the warrior listened to us before attacking.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá tuviéramos otra poción de curación.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wish we had another healing potion.

vocabulary.example: La posada de Frostmarch está llena; ojalá hubiera sitio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The inn in Frostmarch is full; I wish there were room.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá el botín fuera de oro y no de cobre.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If only the loot were gold and not copper.

vocabulary.example: Quisiera entrar en el gremio de magas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'd like to join the mages' guild.

bites.title: Ojalá en Eldmark
bites.rule: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive is the adventurer's sigh for what won't happen: more potions, a sleeping dragon. Quisiera asks the innkeeper nicely.
bites.example_meaning: If only the dragon were asleep.

listening.text: Ojalá fuéramos más fuertes.
listening.meaning: I wish we were stronger.

listening.text: Quisiera una montura para mañana.
listening.meaning: I'd like a mount for tomorrow.
listening.note: New word: la montura = the mount.

listening.text: Ojalá el minotauro no nos viera.
listening.meaning: If only the minotaur didn't see us.

listening.text: Ojalá la maga supiera el camino a Deepanvil.
listening.meaning: I wish the mage knew the way to Deepanvil.

listening.text: El cazador quería que lo esperáramos en Highgate.
listening.meaning: The hunter wanted us to wait for him in Highgate.
listening.note: A past main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive.

builds.meaning: I wish we had more potions.
I'd like to join the guild.

spots.sentence: Ojalá el paladín se poniera la armadura.

sorts.title: Hope or sigh in Eldmark?

items.text: Ojalá el gremio nos pague hoy.
Ojalá el orco hablara mi idioma.

sorts.why: A quest you can still win takes the present subjunctive; a wish against the facts takes the imperfect subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: The dragon is wide awake and staring at you. Ojalá ___ (if only it were asleep).
quiz.explanation: A wish against the facts right now takes the imperfect subjunctive: dormir → durmieron → durmiera. Ojalá never takes the indicative.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá el botín ___ en mi mochila. (caber: if only the loot fitted in my backpack)
quiz.explanation: Caber: cupieron gives cupiera (or cupiese). The backpack is full, so the wish is a long shot.

conversations.title: A full inn in Frostmarch
conversations.scenario: Yrsa, a hunter, reaches the inn at Frostmarch late on a snowy night; Tobías the innkeeper has bad news.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Buenas noches. Quisiera una habitación y algo caliente para cenar.
lines.meaning: Good evening. I'd like a room and something hot for dinner.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ojalá pudiera ayudarte, pero la posada está llena por la feria.
lines.meaning: I wish I could help you, but the inn is full because of the fair.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Vaya! Ojalá no hiciera tanto frío en Frostmarch.
lines.meaning: Oh no! If only it weren't so cold in Frostmarch.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Puedo ofrecerte el establo. Ojalá tuviera algo mejor.
lines.meaning: I can offer you the stable. I wish I had something better.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: El establo me vale. Así duermo con mi montura.
lines.meaning: The stable will do. That way I sleep next to my mount.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Le pedí al gremio que me mandara más camas, pero nada.
lines.meaning: I asked the guild to send me more beds, but nothing.
lines.note: A past main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pues ojalá te hagan caso pronto.
lines.meaning: Well, I hope they listen to you soon.
lines.note: ojalá with the present subjunctive: it can still happen

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ojalá. Toma, una sopa de la casa, y que descanses.
lines.meaning: Let's hope so. Here, a bowl of the house soup, and sleep well.

meadowbrook.content:
## Deseos en Meadowbrook

On the farm, wishes follow the weather. After weeks of sun, **ojalá lloviera** is a sigh, because you doubt it will happen. **Ojalá llueva mañana** sounds hopeful, because the clouds are coming. And at Rosa's seed shop, ask nicely: **Quisiera** semillas de calabaza, por favor.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá las fresas crecieran más rápido.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wish the strawberries grew faster.

vocabulary.example: Quisiera un saco de semillas de maíz, Rosa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'd like a sack of corn seeds, Rosa.

vocabulary.example: Echo de menos el verano; ojalá durara todo el año.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I miss the summer; I wish it lasted all year.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá la vaca me hiciera caso cuando la llamo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If only the cow listened when I call her.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá dispusiera de más tierra para plantar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wish I had more land to plant.

vocabulary.example: Mi deseo para el festival era que vinieran todos los vecinos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My wish for the festival was for all the neighbours to come.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá la cosecha fuera tan buena como la del año pasado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wish the harvest were as good as last year's.

vocabulary.example: Rosa quería que plantara las semillas en primavera.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa wanted me to plant the seeds in spring.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá el huerto fuera más grande.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If only the vegetable garden were bigger.

bites.title: Hope or sigh on the farm
bites.rule: With ojalá, the present subjunctive hopes (ojalá llueva) and the imperfect subjunctive sighs (ojalá lloviera). It is the same wish with less faith.
bites.example_meaning: If only it would rain this week.

listening.text: Ojalá Leo pescara un salmón.
listening.meaning: I wish Leo would catch a salmon.

listening.text: Quisiera vender estas calabazas en el festival.
listening.meaning: I'd like to sell these pumpkins at the festival.

listening.text: Ojalá la mina no estuviera tan lejos.
listening.meaning: If only the mine weren't so far away.

listening.text: Ojalá el granero fuera más grande.
listening.meaning: I wish the barn were bigger.
listening.note: New word: el granero = the barn.

listening.text: El alcalde quería que plantáramos más flores en la plaza.
listening.meaning: The mayor wanted us to plant more flowers in the square.
listening.note: A past main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive.

builds.text: Ojalá las gallinas pusieran más huevos.
builds.meaning: I wish the hens laid more eggs.

builds.text: Quisiera semillas de fresa, por favor.

spots.sentence: Ojalá la vaca me hacería caso.
spots.why: Ojalá takes the subjunctive, never the conditional.

spots.sentence: Ojalá Nora vivíera en el pueblo.
spots.why: Only the nosotros form has a written accent.

sorts.title: Which preterite stem?

items.text: Ojalá hiciera sol en el festival.

sorts.why: The stem comes from the ellos preterite: tuvieron, hicieron, fueron.

quiz.prompt: It's the middle of winter and the fields are frozen. You wish it were summer right now: Ojalá ___ verano.
quiz.explanation: It is winter, so the wish is impossible right now: ojalá + imperfect subjunctive, fuera. Ojalá sea verano makes no sense in January, and era is indicative.
hints: Can it be summer right now?

quiz.prompt: Rosa, ___ un saco de semillas de maíz. (polite 'I'd like', from querer)
quiz.explanation: Quisiera is the polite 'I'd like'. In this use only the -ra form works.

rustwake.content:
## Deseos en el páramo

Out in **el páramo**, everyone sighs **ojalá**: **ojalá tuviera** más tuercas, **ojalá no hubiera** otra tormenta de ceniza. The imperfect subjunctive means you doubt it. At Marta's stall, keep it polite: **Quisiera** dos gaseosas Zafiro.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá el radiorreloj funcionara aquí fuera.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wish the wrist radio worked out here.

vocabulary.example: Quisiera cambiar diez tuercas por agua filtrada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'd like to swap ten nuts for filtered water.

vocabulary.example: Echo de menos la cúpula; ojalá pudiera volver una noche.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I miss the Dome; I wish I could go back for one night.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá me atreviera a explorar el centro comercial en ruinas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wish I dared to explore the ruined shopping centre.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá la armadura de chatarra me cupiera.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If only the scrap armour fitted me.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá dispusiéramos de un taller propio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wish we had a workshop of our own.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá tuviera tuercas suficientes para el tónico.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I wish I had enough nuts for the tonic.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá la tormenta de ceniza pasara pronto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If only the ash storm would pass soon.

vocabulary.example: El capataz Ruiz quería que reparáramos la antena.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Foreman Ruiz wanted us to repair the antenna.

bites.title: Ojalá en el páramo
bites.rule: Out here, ojalá + imperfect subjunctive is for long shots: ojalá encontrara agua limpia. When you trade, ask with quisiera.
bites.example: Quisiera tres tuercas más, por favor.
bites.example_meaning: I'd like three more nuts, please.

listening.text: Ojalá lloviera agua limpia.
listening.meaning: If only clean water would rain down.

listening.text: Quisiera una gaseosa Zafiro bien fría.
listening.meaning: I'd like an ice-cold Zafiro soda.

listening.text: Ojalá el robot jardinero supiera cocinar.
listening.meaning: I wish the gardener robot could cook.

listening.text: Ojalá encontráramos un perro guardián.
listening.meaning: I wish we found a guard dog.
listening.note: New word: el perro guardián = the guard dog.

listening.text: Marta quería que le trajéramos un disco nuevo.
listening.meaning: Marta wanted us to bring her a new record.

builds.meaning: If only the storm would pass soon.
I'd like to swap nuts for water.

spots.why: The nosotros form always takes an accent.

sorts.title: Hope or long shot?

items.text: Ojalá encontremos tuercas en el taller.
Ojalá el páramo fuera verde otra vez.

sorts.why: Present subjunctive for what may really happen; imperfect subjunctive for wishes against the odds.

quiz.explanation: Traer: trajeron → trajera. The j stem of the preterite carries over; traería is the conditional, which never follows ojalá.

quiz.prompt: El capataz Ruiz quería que (nosotros) ___ la antena. (reparar)
quiz.explanation: Quería is in the past, so the imperfect subjunctive follows: repararon → reparáramos (or reparásemos), with the nosotros accent.
